narrative: Severity high, not low or medium: this is not corrected prose, it is a corrected DECISION RATIONALE -- the reason a bound was allowed to rise without further investigation no longer holds, even though the bound's numeric value (59) may still be correct as a measurement. The honest record is that 32->59 was accepted on the strength of a mechanism claim that later instrumentation disproved, and the next person weighing a similar bound-raise-on-a-named-mechanism argument should see that this project has one prior instance where that exact argument turned out to be wrong. observation: D0128's bound-raise ruling (grounded_no_floor 32->59) was justified by an explicit mechanism claim: that the entire 27-violation excess was the already-accepted _grid_floor_backstop/D0059f pit-lip trade-off, reachable at more player-carved locations now that dig exists -- stated in the ledger as 'the same _grid_floor_backstop/D0059f pit-lip trade-off' and by the director's own contemporaneous ruling that raising the bound was acceptable specifically BECAUSE the excess was a known, named, already-accepted mechanism, not an unknown one. D0132's own grounding-path telemetry, built specifically to check this claim, falsifies it: 55/59 dig-on and 29/32 dig-off grounded_no_floor violations trace to resolve_floor, not grid_floor_backstop. The mechanism the bound-raise decision was justified by is not the dominant mechanism in the population the decision covers -- it is a minority contributor (4/59 dig-on, 3/32 dig-off). This is not a refinement of an already-correct attribution; the specific factual claim the decision rested on was wrong, and the instrument built to verify it is what caught this, not a subsequent audit or a change of mind.
